summary: Comprehensive frontend testing of BEARFRAME: GHOST SIGNAL HTML5 canvas game. All 13 feature flows from the review request were exercised through keyboard, DOM click, touch, and the window.__gs debug hook. Every flow worked as specified; no blocking or critical defects found.
critical_code_review_comments: game.js is ~282 lines and mission1.js ~271 lines — both within reasonable size.
input.js correctly uses e.code for KeyboardEvent so layout-independent; last-pressed-wins is enforced via stack.
Scan while flashlight is on drains slightly more than exactly 15 (because flashlight continues per-frame drain). Minor/by-design.
doorC auto-closes when neither player nor ghost is on the plate — matches requirement; combined with lever that locks it open.
Checkpoint restore requires exactly energy <= 0 (not 'low'); drain() clamps to 0 so this works via normal gameplay.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Game is a static site served at http://localhost:3000. Use window.__gs to inspect/manipulate state (player x/y/energy/dir, drone x/y/state/hitCd, flags, ent(id), ghost). Dialogs pause the world; advance with KeyboardEvent code 'KeyE'. Pressing Q right after flashlight test gives ~15.55 drain (expected). For drone-contact test, place drone at (player.x, player.y) and set drone.hitCd=0, drone.invCd=0, drone.blind=0, drone.state='chase'. For zero-energy restore, set player.energy=0 (exactly) — 0.5 won't trigger. Touch mode: set localStorage bearframe_ghost_signal_settings_v1 touch:'on' and reload. All interactive elements have data-testid attributes per index.html.
